assessment_objective: information security-related duties, roles, and responsibilities are assigned to designated personnel.
control_title: Ensure that organizational personnel are adequately trained to carry out their assigned information security-related duties and responsibilities.
rationale: Role assignment IS an enumeration - security roles assigned to personnel emit from the directory/RBAC. The one A&T objective that emits directly.

assessment_objective: personnel are adequately trained to carry out their assigned information security-related duties, roles, and responsibilities.
control_title: Ensure that organizational personnel are adequately trained to carry out their assigned information security-related duties and responsibilities.
rationale: Adequacy of training is a judgment; completion records are process records.

assessment_objective: potential indicators associated with insider threats are identified.
control_title: Provide security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.
rationale: Indicator identification is a determination. Model-content candidate - a Department-published indicator list would discharge it by reference.

assessment_objective: security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat is provided to managers and employees.
control_title: Provide security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.
rationale: Provision of training: LMS completion records attest delivery - process record; content adequacy is human judgment.

assessment_objective: screen individuals prior to authorizing access to organizational systems containing CUI.
control_title: Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to organizational systems containing CUI.
rationale: Screening is a human process performed before access; the screening act does not emit. An HRIS record attests completion - process record. Note: sequencing (screened *prior to* access) could in principle be tested by joining HR dates to account-creation dates, but the HR side is a process record, so the join inherits that status.

assessment_objective: a policy and/or process for terminating system access authorization and any credentials coincident with personnel actions is established.
control_title: Ensure that organizational systems containing CUI are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers.
rationale: Policy/process establishment - a definition objective; no emission. Model-content candidate.

assessment_objective: system access and credentials are terminated consistent with personnel actions such as termination or transfer.
control_title: Ensure that organizational systems containing CUI are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers.
rationale: The system side emits cleanly: account disable/credential revocation events and current account state are directly queryable and joinable to a termination date. What does not emit is the personnel action itself (HR record). Partial: consistency between the two is checkable only if the HR date is supplied - one declared input, then fully machine-checkable. Strongest partial in the set.

assessment_objective: the system is protected during and after personnel transfer actions.
control_title: Ensure that organizational systems containing CUI are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers.
rationale: Access-change state during transfer emits (group membership deltas, permission state); whether the resulting state is *appropriate to the transfer* is judgment. Emission exists, target is undefined.

assessment_objective: system users are identified.
control_title: Identify system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices.
rationale: User identification is the directory itself - the IdP user list is the enumeration.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. V8 AUDIT: IdP list IS the identification. As 03.01.01.a.

assessment_objective: processes acting on behalf of users are identified.
control_title: Identify system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices.
rationale: Service principals and managed identities enumerate cleanly in the cloud path; on-host processes acting for users (service accounts, scheduled tasks) require correlation work. Analyst note concurs: 'will take some work to set up.' Emission exists for the identity layer; completeness across execution contexts is not established.

assessment_objective: devices accessing the system are identified.
control_title: Identify system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices.
rationale: Device registration records are the identification - analyst note: Entra device registration = device identification record.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. V8 AUDIT: Registration record IS the identification. As 03.01.01.c.

assessment_objective: the identity of each user is authenticated or verified as a prerequisite to system access.
control_title: Authenticate or verify the identities of users, processes, or devices, as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational systems.
rationale: Sign-in logs emit every authentication event; CA policy state emits the prerequisite enforcement.

assessment_objective: the identity of each process acting on behalf of a user is authenticated or verified as a prerequisite to system access.
control_title: Authenticate or verify the identities of users, processes, or devices, as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational systems.
rationale: Service-principal sign-ins emit in the cloud path; on-host process authentication (SPN validation, RPC auth per analyst note) emits to security logs but binding every process context to an authenticated identity is not established out of the box.

assessment_objective: the identity of each device accessing or connecting to the system is authenticated or verified as a prerequisite to system access.
control_title: Authenticate or verify the identities of users, processes, or devices, as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational systems.
rationale: Device-based CA (compliant/hybrid-joined required) emits as policy state; device sign-in events emit.

assessment_objective: privileged accounts are identified.
control_title: Use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts.
rationale: Privileged accounts are an enumeration of privileged role/group membership - analyst note concurs.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. V8 AUDIT: Duplicate emission of 03.01.05.a per v7 rationale; lands with it.

assessment_objective: multifactor authentication is implemented for local access to privileged accounts.
control_title: Use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts.
rationale: Local privileged access MFA (smart card / Windows Hello requirement at the host) emits as configuration where enforced; coverage across all local-access paths (safe mode, local console fallback) is not uniformly emitted. Cloud-session MFA is the .c case.

assessment_objective: multifactor authentication is implemented for network access to privileged accounts.
control_title: Use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts.
rationale: CA policy requiring MFA for privileged roles emits as policy state; sign-in logs emit MFA satisfaction per session. Analyst note names the policy.

assessment_objective: multifactor authentication is implemented for network access to non-privileged accounts.
control_title: Use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts.
rationale: As .c at broader scope.

assessment_objective: employ replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for network access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
control_title: Employ replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for network access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
rationale: Authentication-strength policy (FIDO2/WHfB) emits as CA configuration; replay resistance is a property of the enforced method class. Analyst note concurs.

assessment_objective: a period within which identifiers cannot be reused is defined.
control_title: Prevent reuse of identifiers for a defined period.
rationale: Identifier-reuse window emits as tenant setting (soft-delete retention period). Definition floor question separate per scoping.
change_note: V8.8: referent is April 2025 DoD ODP 03.05.05.c (owner ruling). V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. FLOOR RULE: reuse-prevention period is a scalar; no confirmed Department value. Pending ODP pass.

assessment_objective: reuse of identifiers is prevented within the defined period.
control_title: Prevent reuse of identifiers for a defined period.
rationale: Soft-deleted object state and restoration window emit; uniqueness constraints enforced by the directory itself.

assessment_objective: a period of inactivity after which an identifier is disabled is defined.
control_title: Disable identifiers after a defined period of inactivity.
rationale: Inactivity-disable period emits as policy configuration where the policy exists. Analyst flag retained: automated enforcement requires P2 or custom script - license-tier dependency.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. FLOOR RULE: inactivity-disable period scalar; pending ODP pass. License-tier note retained.

assessment_objective: identifiers are disabled after the defined period of inactivity.
control_title: Disable identifiers after a defined period of inactivity.
rationale: Last-sign-in timestamps and account-enabled state are queryable; disabled-after-inactivity is a join.

assessment_objective: password complexity requirements are defined.
control_title: Enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created.
rationale: Password policy configuration emits (AD policy / Entra password protection / pwquality).
change_note: Authority recorded: benchmark specifies password policy values. | V8 AUDIT: KEPT: double-floored (benchmark values + 03.05.07.f length 16).

assessment_objective: password change of character requirements are defined.
control_title: Enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created.
rationale: Change-of-character requirement emits as configuration (pwquality difok per analyst note) on the Linux path; Windows path lacks a native equivalent setting - path-dependent, noted.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. V8 AUDIT: Scope contradiction: Windows lacks native change-of-character setting; pwquality difok is Linux-path and Linux endpoints excluded from reference architecture. No emission on declared path; retained partial pending Entra password-protection verification.

assessment_objective: minimum password complexity requirements as defined are enforced when new passwords are created.
control_title: Enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created.
rationale: Enforcement is the policy engine itself; rejection events emit.

assessment_objective: minimum password change of character requirements as defined are enforced when new passwords are created.
control_title: Enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created.
rationale: As .b - enforced where the mechanism exists; path-dependent.

assessment_objective: the number of generations during which a password cannot be reused is specified.
control_title: Prohibit password reuse for a specified number of generations.
rationale: Password-history depth emits as policy setting.
change_note: Authority recorded: benchmark specifies history depth. | V8 AUDIT: KEPT: benchmark specifies history depth; policy emits.

assessment_objective: reuse of passwords is prohibited during the specified number of generations.
control_title: Prohibit password reuse for a specified number of generations.
rationale: History enforcement is the policy engine; setting state is the emission.

assessment_objective: allow temporary password use for system logons with an immediate change to a permanent password.
control_title: Allow temporary password use for system logons with an immediate change to a permanent password
rationale: Temporary-access-pass config (cloud) or must-change-at-next-logon flag (on-prem) emit. Analyst note marks path-dependence; both paths emit.

assessment_objective: passwords are cryptographically protected in storage.
control_title: Store and transmit only cryptographically-protected passwords.
rationale: Storage protection is an OS implementation property (hashing in AD/SAM, /etc/shadow). What emits is the configuration surrounding it (e.g. reversible-encryption disabled, shadow permissions); the cryptographic property itself is asserted by platform design rather than emitted. Partial: config emits, the protected property is inherited from the OS vendor's implementation.

assessment_objective: passwords are cryptographically protected in transit.
control_title: Store and transmit only cryptographically-protected passwords.
rationale: Transit protection emits as protocol configuration - TLS/LDAPS enforcement, NTLM restrictions, Kerberos encryption types are all readable settings.

assessment_objective: obscure feedback of authentication information.
control_title: Obscure feedback of authentication information.
rationale: Feedback obscuring (password masking, lock-screen credential hiding) emits as OS policy settings covered by the benchmark.

assessment_objective: the time within which to identify system flaws is specified.
control_title: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
rationale: Scan schedule configuration IS the specified timeframe - analyst note: DEFINE_AS_SETTING. The emission is the schedule; whether a formal window is also documented is the floor question, kept separate.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. FLOOR RULE: scan-timeframe scalar; schedule emits but ratifies itself absent a published window. Pending ODP pass. Note 03.14.01.e finding: published remediation windows would convert the pair.

assessment_objective: system flaws are identified within the specified time frame.
control_title: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
rationale: Scan execution records and finding timestamps emit; identification-within-timeframe is a join of finding date to schedule.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. V8 AUDIT: Identification-within-timeframe: R2 3.14.1[a] makes the timeframe org-specified; R3 30/90/180 values floor REMEDIATION (3.14.1[e]/[f] analog), a different parameter. Emission real (finding timestamps vs schedule); floor not published.

assessment_objective: the time within which to report system flaws is specified.
control_title: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
rationale: Reporting timeframe is a determination with no configuration surface in the lab stack - no setting encodes 'report within N days.' Definition objective, no emission.

assessment_objective: system flaws are reported within the specified time frame.
control_title: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
rationale: Alert/notification records emit when findings route to owners; that this constitutes 'reporting' per a specified timeframe requires the .c definition to exist. Emission of the routing event is real; the target is undefined.

assessment_objective: the time within which to correct system flaws is specified.
control_title: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
rationale: Correction timeframe is documented (SSP per analyst note - BOD 22-01 values) but no system setting encodes it; the value lives in prose. Definition objective, no emission. Note: if the Department published remediation-window ODPs, .e would be discharged by reference and .f would become a pure join - the clearest single instance of a publishable value converting a definition pair.

assessment_objective: system flaws are corrected within the specified time frame.
control_title: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
rationale: Vulnerability state over time emits (first-seen/last-seen per finding); time-to-remediate is a query. Checkable against any supplied window.
change_note: V8.7: yes->no. Owner ruling (SIEM tiering). assessment_objective: designated locations for malicious code protection are identified.
control_title: Provide protection from malicious code at designated locations within organizational systems.
rationale: Deployment state of protection agents emits per endpoint; whether deployed locations constitute the 'designated' set requires the designation - declared-input pattern, as 03.09.02.b.

assessment_objective: protection from malicious code at designated locations is provided.
control_title: Provide protection from malicious code at designated locations within organizational systems.
rationale: AV/EDR enabled-state, engine and platform versions emit per device.

assessment_objective: response actions to system security alerts and advisories are identified.
control_title: Monitor system security alerts and advisories and take action in response.
rationale: Response-action identification is a determination (playbook content); no emission. Model-content candidate - advisory-response actions are largely common across suppliers.

assessment_objective: system security alerts and advisories are monitored.
control_title: Monitor system security alerts and advisories and take action in response.
rationale: Advisory-feed ingestion emits where a threat-intel connector is configured; monitoring of advisories outside integrated feeds (vendor bulletins, CISA emails) does not emit. Lab stack has partial feed integration.

assessment_objective: actions in response to system security alerts and advisories are taken.
control_title: Monitor system security alerts and advisories and take action in response.
rationale: Automated response actions emit execution records (analyst note: Active Response is the mechanism); human response actions are process records. Split by action class.

assessment_objective: update malicious code protection mechanisms when new releases are available.
control_title: Update malicious code protection mechanisms when new releases are available.
rationale: Signature/engine currency emits per endpoint - version and last-update timestamp are readable state; update-on-release is a comparison to vendor-current.

assessment_objective: the frequency for malicious code scans is defined.
control_title: Perform periodic scans of organizational systems and real-time scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed.
rationale: Scan frequency emits as configuration. Definition floor separate.
change_note: V8.8: referent is April 2025 DoD ODP 03.14.02.c.01 (owner ruling). V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. FLOOR RULE: scan-frequency scalar; pending ODP pass.

assessment_objective: malicious code scans are performed with the defined frequency.
control_title: Perform periodic scans of organizational systems and real-time scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed.
rationale: Scan execution records emit; performed-per-frequency is a join.

assessment_objective: real-time malicious code scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed are performed.
control_title: Perform periodic scans of organizational systems and real-time scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed.
rationale: Real-time protection state emits as setting (on-access scanning enabled).

assessment_objective: the system is monitored to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.
control_title: Monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks
rationale: Monitoring coverage emits: agent deployment state plus alert pipeline. That monitoring is *occurring* is the emission; detection efficacy is not claimed.

assessment_objective: inbound communications traffic is monitored to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.
control_title: Monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks
rationale: Inbound traffic monitoring emits where network sensors/firewall logs are integrated; lab stack integrates host-level but not full network-boundary capture. Partial on deployed coverage in the reference environment.

assessment_objective: outbound communications traffic is monitored to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.
control_title: Monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks
rationale: As .b for outbound - egress monitoring coverage is partial in the lab stack.

assessment_objective: authorized use of the system is defined.
control_title: Identify unauthorized use of organizational systems.
rationale: The Conditional Access / RBAC / session-policy ruleset natively encodes the definition of authorized use for a general support system: who, from what device posture, under what conditions, to which functions. Definition-as-setting; same emission also evidences 3.1.1/3.1.2 (cross-family, as 03.01.05.a/03.05.03.a). No published referent for what the definition must include -> artifact, not yes. No conduct/AUP gate: no published value requires one.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. V8.1 PROMOTION (no -> artifact): first row to enter the reportable set across four audit passes. Owner ruling: for a GSS, authorized use IS access; encoded ruleset is the enforceable definition.

assessment_objective: unauthorized use of the system is identified.
control_title: Identify unauthorized use of organizational systems.

change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. assessment_objective: authorized users are identified.
control_title: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices
rationale: The IdP user list is the identification. Analyst note suggests prose plus ID-validation pointer; under the emission test the enumeration itself is the artifact - validation rigor is a floor question, kept separate.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. assessment_objective: processes acting on behalf of authorized users are identified.
control_title: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices
rationale: As 03.05.01.b - service principals enumerate cleanly; on-host process contexts require correlation. Same split, same reason.

assessment_objective: devices (including other systems) authorized to connect to the system are identified.
control_title: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices
rationale: Device inventory is the identification - analyst note concurs (Entra device records; AD computer objects on the traditional path).
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. V8 AUDIT: Device inventory IS the identification; "authorized to connect" judgment not emitted. As .a.

assessment_objective: system access is limited to authorized users.
control_title: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices
rationale: Analyst note: the CA policy gate IS the authorization enforcement. Policy state emits; sign-in logs emit every allow/deny decision.

assessment_objective: system access is limited to processes acting on behalf of authorized users.
control_title: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices
rationale: Service principals and app registrations define authorized processes (analyst note); both enumerate.

assessment_objective: system access is limited to authorized devices (including other systems).
control_title: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices
rationale: Compliant-device CA condition emits as policy state; device record is the authorization list. ODP present (90-day currency).
change_note: Authority recorded: ODP fixes device-currency window (90 days).

assessment_objective: the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute are defined
control_title: Limit system access to the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute.
rationale: RBAC role definitions ARE the enumeration of permitted transaction and function types: actions/notActions lists, app-role assignments, CA conditions. The most literal definition-as-setting instance in the set; same artifact as 03.14.07.a read at content level. No published referent for what the permitted set must contain -> artifact.
change_note: V8.8: promoted partial->yes. Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. V8.2 PROMOTION (no -> artifact): owner ruling — same artifact as 03.14.07.a, examined twice. Cross-family single-emission pattern.

assessment_objective: system access is limited to the defined types of transactions and functions for authorized users.
control_title: Limit system access to the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute.
rationale: App-level CA conditions, named locations, session controls emit; enforcement target is now the encoded role-definition/CA set of .a (artifact). Partial: referent customer-authored.
change_note: V8.2: target repaired — upstream definitional row promoted to artifact. Disposition unchanged.

assessment_objective: information flow control policies are defined.
control_title: Control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations.
rationale: Flow-control policy definition is an architectural determination; no emission. Design-definition class.

assessment_objective: methods and enforcement mechanisms for controlling the flow of CUI are defined.
control_title: Control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations.
rationale: The NSG/private-endpoint/transport rule set is simultaneously the flow-control mechanism and its definition. Sibling .d has held this exact rationale since v7 ("rules natively encode the authorizations"); .b is the same sentence at mechanism level.

Referent is the organization-defined value the standard obliges the organization to set; validation executes against it when the export carries the declaration and the observation as separate assertions. assessment_objective: designated sources and destinations (e.g., networks, individuals, and devices) for CUI within systems and between interconnected systems are identified.
control_title: Control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations.
rationale: Network topology (NSGs, peering) and inventory partially enumerate designated sources/destinations; the designation act - which of these carry CUI - is a declaration. Declared-input pattern.

assessment_objective: authorizations for controlling the flow of CUI are defined.
control_title: Control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations.
rationale: Analyst note is exactly right and worth quoting: NSG rules = network-layer authorization expression; CA = identity-layer; transport rules = mail flow. The authorizations exist AS configuration - the rare definition objective where the definition is natively machine-encoded.

assessment_objective: approved authorizations for controlling the flow of CUI are enforced.

rationale: Enforcement state is the same rule sets as .d, plus flow logs emit permit/deny decisions.

assessment_objective: the duties of individuals requiring separation to reduce the risk of malevolent activity are defined.
control_title: Separate the duties of individuals to reduce the risk of malevolent activity without collusion.
rationale: Separation-of-duties definition is an organizational determination (which roles conflict); no emission. Analyst proposes an SoD matrix - that matrix would be a declared input, not an emission.

assessment_objective: organization-defined duties of individuals requiring separation are separated.
control_title: Separate the duties of individuals to reduce the risk of malevolent activity without collusion.
rationale: Role assignments enumerate; verifying *separation* requires the .a conflict matrix. Given the matrix, the check is a pure join - declared-input pattern, as 03.09.02.b.

assessment_objective: separate accounts for individuals whose duties and accesses must be separated to reduce the risk of malevolent activity or collusion are established

assessment_objective: privileged accounts are identified.

assessment_objective: access to privileged accounts is authorized in accordance with the principle of least privilege.

assessment_objective: security functions are identified.

One notch more inferential than 03.01.07.a — the identification is carried by what the benchmark governs rather than a captioned list — stated here for the record.

assessment_objective: access to security functions is authorized in accordance with the principle of least privilege.
control_title: Employ the principle of least privilege, including for specific security functions and privileged accounts.
rationale: Least-privilege access to security functions is rights-assignment conformance against benchmark-recommended values — the canonical User Rights compliance scan. Blocker removed by the .c promotion: the referent is now published content.
